blocks.note: cove is old slang for a chap or fellow
R for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A bodyguard arrangement: a man walks ahead of the Queen to keep her safe.
explanation.walkthrough: Cove is a dated British word for a man, common in crosswords; R stands for Regina, as on royal cyphers.
explanation.definitionFit: Cover means shelter or a shield from danger, as in taking cover under fire.

indicators.note: what is swallowed ends up inside the swallower

blocks.note: to charter a boat or plane is to lease it
AC is the standard abbreviation for account

explanation.surface: Legal paperwork about a building, where one account has been absorbed into the terms of a tenancy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Property' looks like real estate, which chimes with 'lease', but here it means a quality or trait, as in the properties of a metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A property of something is a distinguishing trait or feature, which is what its character describes.

clue.text: Lines going inside through country house

blocks.note: via means by way of, through
L is line, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Telephone or power lines being run through a rural mansion.
explanation.walkthrough: LL for 'lines' is a crossword convention: one L per line, as in reference citations.
explanation.definitionFit: A villa is a large rural residence, originally a Roman estate with its farm buildings.

clue.text: English love sailor climbing some rigging

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means reading from bottom to top, so the string is turned round

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
love is a zero score in tennis, and nil is zero
a tar (jack tar) is a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor with a sweetheart in England shinning up the rigging of a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's climbing sailor is the neat touch: ratlines are exactly what sailors climb, and 'climbing' also reverses the string in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratlines are the small rope rungs across a ship's shrouds, forming ladders; they are one part of its rigging.

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for husband in genealogy tables
e is the base of natural logarithms
artless means simple, without guile

explanation.surface: A scathing verdict on a husband: low, simple-minded and cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Base' reads as an insult alongside 'simple', but it is the mathematical constant e, the base of natural logs.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone heartless shows no compassion or emotion, which is exactly to be callous and cold.

clue.text: The man excelled keeping sweetheart inclined

indicators.note: the heart of the word sweet is its centre letter, so only that middle one is kept

blocks.note: he is the pronoun for 'the man'
the middle letter of sweet
to have led is to have been out in front, to have excelled

explanation.surface: A man who did well while keeping his girlfriend happy, and so was well disposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweetheart' pretends to be a lover; in crosswords it often means the heart of 'sweet', one E.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship that has heeled over is tilted or leaning to one side, so it is inclined.

clue.text: Radio set tuned finding celestial body

blocks.note: anagram fodder, eight letters

explanation.surface: Someone twiddling a radio dial and picking up a signal from a heavenly object, as radio astronomers do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Radio set' reads as one object, the wireless, but it is the fodder and 'tuned' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: An asteroid is a small rocky planet-like object orbiting the sun, one kind of heavenly body.

indicators.note: 'of' tells the solver the answer is made out of the words that follow, lying across them

blocks.note: the letters run from the last of Government through ran into the start of Chequers

explanation.surface: A political note: a department of government that ran the Prime Minister's country residence.
explanation.walkthrough: Chequers is the country house of the British Prime Minister, so the surface feels political; the answer runs across 'GovernmenT RAN CHEquers'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tranche is a portion or slice of something larger, such as one release of funding.

clue.text: Development in love, out at sea

indicators.note: to be at sea is to be confused and all over the place, so those letters are jumbled

blocks.note: anagram fodder, nine letters

explanation.surface: A romance that blossoms while the couple are away on a voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface splits into 'in love' and 'out at sea', but the fodder is the three words 'in love, out' together.
explanation.definitionFit: Evolution is gradual change and growth over time, which is what a development is.

blocks.note: a sin is a transgression
the first and last letters of chastise

explanation.surface: A parent's instruction to scold a wrongdoer coldly once the misdeed is done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' sits at the front looking like a link to the wordplay; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Since as a preposition means from a point in time onward, as in 'since the war', so later than.

indicators.note: one word goes round, about, another

blocks.note: all is everything
OTT, over the top, means exaggerated
men are males

explanation.surface: A complaint that men have blown everything out of proportion when sharing it out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over the top' is British slang for excessive, abbreviated in crosswords to its three initials.
explanation.definitionFit: An allotment is the portion allocated to someone, their allowance or part of the whole.

blocks.note: ado is fuss or commotion
RN is the Royal Navy, the sailors

explanation.surface: A disturbance among the crew up on the ship's deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deck' and 'sailors' make a nautical picture, but deck is the verb to decorate.
explanation.definitionFit: To deck a hall with holly is to decorate or embellish it, which is to adorn it.

clue.text: Greed, a weakness gripping a Republican

blocks.note: the article as printed
a vice is a moral weakness
the second article as printed
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: A political jibe: greed is the one failing that has a certain Republican in its grip.
explanation.walkthrough: The article 'a' appears twice and is used both times, once at the front and once inside the weakness.
explanation.definitionFit: Avarice is an extreme desire for wealth or gain, one of the seven deadly sins.

clue.text: Monk left Church repelled in deception

indicators.note: what is repelled is driven back

blocks.note: L for left
CE is the Church of England
a ruse is a trick or deception

explanation.surface: A monk who has walked out of the Church, driven off by its deceit.
explanation.walkthrough: CE, the Church of England, is a common crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A recluse lives in seclusion, as religious hermits and some monks do, withdrawn from society.

indicators.note: to embody something is to take it into your body

blocks.note: tries means attempts or struggles
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A cynic's view of a political party: all its infighting stands for nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tories are Britain's Conservative Party; the plural 'Tories' stands for the party as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Tories is the common name for members of the British Conservative Party, and so for the party itself.

clue.text: Recover from illnesses, so perhaps rising

indicators.note: the answer is taken out from the run of words that follows
in a down clue rising reads upward, bottom to top, so the hidden run is backwards

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of illnesses, through so, into the start of perhaps

explanation.surface: Someone getting over their ailments and, it seems, getting back on their feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recover from illnesses' reads as one medical phrase; 'Recover' is the definition, and the answer is reversed in 'illnESSES SO PERhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: To repossess goods is to take them back when payments stop, a financial way of recovering them.

blocks.note: surface reading: people astonished or overwhelmed, bowled over by something
setter's reading: objects literally knocked down by a thrown ball, as the point of a skittles game

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bowled over' usually means amazed; here it is literal, and the pins falling over are the game.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninepins is a skittles game in which nine wooden pins are knocked down with a ball, and the pins themselves.

clue.text: Shrewd, keeping quietly fit and active

blocks.note: sly means cunning, shrewd
p is piano, the musical instruction to play quietly
right means suitable or fit, as in the right person for the job

explanation.surface: A portrait of a canny person who quietly keeps in good shape and stays on the move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fit and active' looks like one health phrase; 'fit' is wordplay and 'active' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprightly describes someone lively and energetic, especially an older person, so active and brisk.

blocks.note: surface reading: something that helps a person who is taking a nap
setter's reading: napper is British slang for the head, so this is a prop for that part of the body

explanation.walkthrough: Napper is old British slang for the head; the clue also suits a dozer, since you lean back on one to nap.
explanation.definitionFit: A headrest is a cushioned pad on a seat that holds up the back of a passenger's skull.

blocks.note: a reed is a tall grass
peat is dug and burnt as fuel

explanation.surface: A gardener's discovery that ordinary fuel keeps turning up among the grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' can also mean an informer in British slang, but here it is simply the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Something repeated happens again and again at intervals, so it is recurring or regular.

blocks.note: to aver is to state or declare
to age is to grow old and decline

explanation.surface: A reassurance, perhaps from a doctor or economist, that some deterioration is to be expected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a noun, a country or condition, but it is the verb to declare.
explanation.definitionFit: Average means typical or ordinary, the usual standard, which is what normal describes.

blocks.note: a tenor is a male singer, and said out loud it matches the banknote

explanation.surface: A singer using his voice to hit a musical note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singer' and 'note' set up a musical scene; the note is money. A tenner is British slang for a ten-pound banknote.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenner is slang for a ten-pound banknote, so it is a note in the money sense.

clue.text: Strange one with a rum charm

indicators.note: strange means odd and out of order, so the letters that follow are jumbled

blocks.note: anagram fodder: one, a and rum, seven letters

explanation.surface: An odd person holding a glass of rum and a lucky talisman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rum' looks like a second anagram signal, since it means odd, but here it is fodder; 'with' only joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To enamour someone is to captivate them and fill them with love, which is to charm them.

blocks.note: an hour is a time or occasion, as in 'the hour has come'
an actor who is on is performing on stage

explanation.surface: An actor on stage at a gala event, performing to win a prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Occasion' is a stretch for a time of day, but the hour of something is its moment, as in 'the hour has come'.
explanation.definitionFit: An honour is a title or decoration given in recognition, such as a knighthood, so it is an award.

clue.text: Detectives are liable to get stretch

blocks.note: DIs are Detective Inspectors
they tend to means they are liable to

explanation.surface: Police officers who, being liable, may end up serving a prison sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stretch' looks like prison slang for a sentence, fitting the detectives; it is the verb to swell. DI is Detective Inspector.
explanation.definitionFit: To distend is to swell or expand outwards from internal pressure, making something stretch.

blocks.note: the second and fourth letters of admit
hot means sexy

explanation.surface: A confession that one sometimes buys revealing underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Purchasing' reads as buying but it is a container signal, from purchase meaning a grip. A dhoti is the loincloth worn by Hindu men in India.
explanation.definitionFit: A dhoti is a length of cloth wrapped around the waist and legs, a traditional Indian garment for men.

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for ordinary
a rating is a sailor below officer rank

explanation.surface: An ordinary seaman boldly departing on a voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setting forth' suggests a sailor setting out to sea; it means declaring opinions. A rating is a naval sailor who is not an officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Orating is making a formal speech, often pompously, so expounding views with force and conviction.

clue.text: Individual deeply imbecilic or thick, initially

definitions.text: Individual deeply imbecilic or thick, initially

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of each preceding word is kept

blocks.note: the first letters of the five words

explanation.surface: A blunt description of someone profoundly foolish and slow-witted.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: its first letters spell the answer, and read straight it describes one.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiot is a stupid person, and calling someone deeply imbecilic and thick describes exactly that.

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
mega means huge, colossal

explanation.surface: An ancient giant figure from Greek myth, perhaps the Colossus of Rhodes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' suggests a person from legend; it is a letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the last letter of the Greek alphabet, and a letter is a written character.

indicators.note: to redistribute is to share out again in a new way, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: anagram fodder, nine letters

explanation.surface: A policy proposal: share out earnings more evenly and hand them to a specialist in money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To' looks like a link word, but it supplies the last two letters of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An economist studies how wealth, money and resources are produced and used, a specialist in that field.

clue.text: One script rewritten for Morse, maybe

indicators.note: a rewritten text has been recast, so these letters come out in a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, nine letters

explanation.surface: A screenwriter redrafting an episode of the television detective series Morse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Morse' suggests the code; it is Inspector Morse, the Oxford detective of Colin Dexter's novels and the ITV series.
explanation.definitionFit: Morse is a fictional police detective whose rank is inspector, so he is one example of the rank.

blocks.note: a ray is a streak of light
the TT, Tourist Trophy, is the motorcycle race on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A racer on a winning streak who is itching to get going.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT is the Isle of Man Tourist Trophy motorcycle race, a crossword staple. Ratty is British informal for irritable.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratty is British slang for irritable and short-tempered, close to being impatient and tetchy.
